steps.name: Phase 2: build cvesByHost reverse-join map, enrich endpoints, emit hydrated rows
Port mapper helpers (MapAsset, MapVulnerabilityFromCve, BuildCvesByHost, BuildFindingId, ResolveCveName) into a collector-local helper class
Remove dead helpers (isDatasetReadyForQuery, findDataset, isDatasetExplicitlyEmpty, plus any others rendered unreachable)
Update CortexXdrCollector/Examples/README.md 'Known asymmetry' (or defer via execution_notes.md)
dotnet build clean; existing collector tests pass

assumptions.summary: FetchEndpointsAsync paginates last_seen DESC, stops at last_seen < baseDate; reuse with iIsDryRun?UtcNow:iBaseDate
FetchXqlResultsAsync sends no timeframe; va_cves XQL is unbounded by design
Reverse-join va_cves.affected_hosts[] ↔ endpoint.endpoint_name is case-insensitive; validated against probe archive CortexXdr_20260514_080340_616Z
CollectAssetsAsync keeps forward-join finding_ids[]; id-set asymmetry with new findings flow is accepted
cvesByHost ~75 MB heap ceiling acceptable per operator but unverified under production memory pressure
Tenants without Host Insights return zero va_cves rows; readiness gate misclassifies — dropping it is correct

decisions.summary: Refactor scope is CollectFindingsAsync plus dead-helper cleanup; CollectAssetsAsync untouched
Defender-style intermediates: cves.jsonl + endpoints.jsonl to per-collection temp dir; enrich in Phase 2
cvesByHost is an in-memory Dictionary<string, List<JObject>>, case-insensitive hostname key
Drop /xql/get_datasets readiness gate and unreachable helpers
baseDate gates endpoints pagination only; va_cves XQL stays unbounded
Port mapper logic byte-faithfully into a collector-local helper (e.g. CortexXdrFindingsMapper)
Direct execution path (single contributor, focused refactor, no decomposition)
